column1: # Running a machine's system activation is the operator's switch gesture: it changes what runs, as root, and on a
# seat it can reach tart:vm:factory-reset:apply, whose rm -rf destroys a guest's disks (its Incus DB included). The
# sessions have passwordless sudo here, so the deny hook is the only barrier. Columns, tab-separated: want
# (DENY|ALLOW), today (bad62b2a's hook, measured), cwd (- for /tmp/work), cmd. A case is loosened only with 🛡️'s review.
# The activation script itself, by every path a system profile reaches it.
# NixOS: the switch program inside a system closure.
# Behind a launcher, a shell or a prefix.
# Pointing the system profile at another closure is half of a switch.
# Setting the factory-reset variable at all, for any command.
# Already refused: the darwin-rebuild front door (kept so a rewrite keeps them).
# Reading an activation script, or listing a profile, changes nothing.
# The indirections (🛡️, 2026-10-25). A file named activate, activate-user or switch-to-configuration is refused BY
# NAME, whatever path reaches it: a symlink made earlier in the same command hides the closure from the hook, and on
# a no-rollback path with passwordless sudo a false refusal is cheap while a miss costs a guest's disks.
# An OPAQUE PROGRAM under sudo: a variable or a substitution in the PROGRAM position. With passwordless sudo this is a
# root command the hook cannot judge at all, a blind spot for EVERY refusal, not only activation. Decided: refused.
# Writing the path out literally is the way. Arguments stay free: only the program position is judged.
# Reading an activate script, by any path, changes nothing.
# A root shell fed its program from STDIN or by xargs (🛡️, 2026-10-25): the hook can't read what it runs, the same
# blind feed as an opaque program under sudo, one level down. Refused when the shell gets no script or -c to judge.
# Still judged, so allowed: a root shell given -c with a literal the hook reads.
# xargs feeding sudo ANY program is refused already (the opaque-program rule): what it runs on comes from stdin.
